bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42491975 (htslib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target hts_open_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42491975
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's heap-buffer-overflow while opening the staged 207-byte CRAM 2.1 witness with `hts_open_fuzzer`. The first CRAM header block that `cram_read_SAM_hdr()` reads is parsed as a compressed `RANS_PR0` block with `b->comp_size = 2`, so `cram_read_block()` allocates a 2-byte heap buffer and `cram_uncompress_block()` dispatches it to `rans_uncompress_4x16()`. Inside `rans_uncompress_to_4x16()`, the first payload byte sets `X_STRIPE`, which puts the decoder on the striped metadata path with `c_meta_len = 1`. `var_get_u32(in + 1, in_end, &ulen)` then consumes the only remaining byte and advances `c_meta_len` to 2, exactly `in_size`. Vulnerable code immediately executes `unsigned int N = in[c_meta_len++]` without the post-varint bound check added by the staged patch, so the `N` load dereferences `in[2]` one byte past the 2-byte allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `READ of size 1` at `rANS_static4x16pr.c:1536`, and the patch fixes this exact obligation by inserting `if (c_meta_len >= in_size) return NULL;` before the `N` read.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled compressed block descriptor. This statement sequence materializes the decoder dispatch key (`b->method`) and compressed extent (`b->comp_size`) for the first CRAM header block that later crashes in rANS decoding.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 207-byte CRAM 2.1 file. In the reproduced Stage 01 crash, the later stack proves this parsed block reaches `cram_uncompress_block()` as `RANS_PR0`, and the allocation context at `cram_read_block()` line 1445 proves the parsed `b->comp_size` for that same block is `2`.
source.note: Source. These header fields are the first project-code state derived from the witness that decide both which decompressor runs and how many bytes it may read.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. With `c_meta_len == in_size == 2`, this byte load dereferences one byte past the 2-byte compressed block buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at this exact line, and the allocation stack points back to the 2-byte `malloc` in `cram_read_block()`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After `var_get_u32()` consumes the last available striped-metadata byte, the code still performs this `N` read without first enforcing the missing `c_meta_len >= in_size` guard.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (c_meta_len >= in_size) return NULL;` immediately before this line, confirming that the post-`ulen` bounds check was the missing obligation.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled compressed-size field that later becomes both the heap allocation extent in `cram_read_block()` and the `in_size` bound handed to `rans_uncompress_to_4x16()`.

parser_admitted.description: The input has already passed CRAM file-definition and first-container parsing. `cram_read_SAM_hdr()` is now decompressing the first header block, which is the exact parser path that reaches the vulnerable rANS decoder.

evidence_limitations: The sample metadata points at htscodecs commits, while Stage 01 reproduced the crash in a staged htslib checkout with a bundled htscodecs submodule. All source locations above use the exact staged workspace line map (`htslib` commit `01830d77854bf24d69959373d2570c640c1ff5d2`, bundled `htscodecs` commit `dca826bbc598d6dcae450e92e60dcf789454999d`).

The malformed CRAM bytes preceding the crashing block were not fully reconstructed field-by-field from the raw witness. The trigger contract is therefore anchored to the runtime-verified block properties from Stage 01 (`RANS_PR0`, `b->comp_size == 2`, striped path taken) plus the exact vulnerable source logic, which are the load-bearing facts for this crash.

fine_trace.note: Source. `cram_read_block()` parses the first attacker-controlled header block descriptor. In the reproduced crash, this parse materializes a compressed `RANS_PR0` block whose `b->comp_size` is `2`, which determines both the decoder dispatch and the compressed-buffer extent.

Because this is a compressed block, the parsed `b->comp_size` becomes the heap allocation extent. For the crashing witness this allocates `malloc(2)` and reads exactly those 2 attacker-controlled bytes into `b->data`; ASan's allocation stack lands on this `malloc`.
The parsed compression method selects the `RANS_PR0` branch, so the same 2-byte heap buffer from step 2 is passed to `rans_uncompress_4x16()` with `in_size = b->comp_size = 2`.

fine_trace.code:
if (*in & X_STRIPE) {
    unsigned int ulen, olen, c_meta_len = 1;
fine_trace.note: The first compressed-byte option word has `X_STRIPE` set, so the decoder enters the striped metadata path with `c_meta_len = 1`. The only earlier size guard in this function is `if (in_size == 0) return NULL;`; with `in_size == 2`, exactly one byte remains for striped metadata.

With only one byte between `in + 1` and `in_end`, `var_get_u32()` consumes that sole remaining byte and advances `c_meta_len` from `1` to `2`. The striped metadata cursor now equals `in_size` before the stream-count byte `N` is loaded.

Root cause. After step 5, `c_meta_len` is already `2`, but the code still falls through to this `N` load without the missing `if (c_meta_len >= in_size) return NULL;` guard. The staged patch inserts exactly that check before this line.

Sink. Evaluating `in[c_meta_len]` dereferences `in[2]` while `in` still aliases the 2-byte heap buffer from step 2, so the read crosses one byte past the allocation. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line.

poc.trigger: Opening the staged 207-byte CRAM 2.1 witness with `hts_open_fuzzer` makes `cram_read_SAM_hdr()` uncompress a 2-byte `RANS_PR0` header block whose striped metadata ends before the `N` byte, triggering the ASan heap-buffer-overflow read in `rans_uncompress_to_4x16()`.

format.name: CRAM 2.1
format.contract: The exact witness is a 207-byte CRAM 2.1 file whose first CRAM header block is parsed as `RANS_PR0` with `b->comp_size == 2`, and whose 2-byte compressed payload has `in[0] & X_STRIPE` set so `rans_uncompress_to_4x16()` enters the striped path, consumes the only remaining byte in `var_get_u32(in + 1, in_end, &ulen)`, and has no following byte available for `N`.
